name: Senganmal Ranganatha Perumal Temple, Thiruthetriyambalam
deity: Vishnu as Pallikonda Perumal, Senganmal Ranganatha, reclining on Adisesha, with Sengamalavalli Thayar — Thiruthetriyambalam, the reclining Lord among the eleven Thirunangur Divya Desams
period: A Divya Desam of Chola Nadu, one of the eleven Thirunangur shrines, sung by Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
summary: At Thirunangur near Sirkazhi, Vishnu reclines on Adisesha as Senganmal Ranganatha, the red-eyed Lord — the only reclining form among the eleven Thirunangur Divya Desams, sung by Thirumangai Alvar beside the Surya Pushkarini.

sections.history: Thiruthetriyambalam is one of the 108 Divya Desams and lies in Chola Nadu, at Thirunangur east of Sirkazhi. It is one of the eleven Vishnu shrines of Thirunangur, each sung by Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, and it is the only one of the eleven in which the Lord reclines. He is Pallikonda Perumal, also called Senganmal, 'the red-eyed Lord', Ranganathar and Sri Lakshmi Rangar, lying on Adisesha with four arms, facing east, with Sridevi near his head and Bhudevi at his feet. The shrine is often noted as the only Perumal temple in Tamil Nadu with the title ambalam in its name. The Alvar's hymn places it in the eighth century.
sections.architecture: The sanctum is crowned by the Veda vimana. Within it the Lord lies in the sayana thirukkolam on the serpent Adisesha, with his consorts at head and feet, in the manner of the great reclining Ranganatha shrines. Sengamalavalli Thayar has her own shrine. The temple tank is the Surya Pushkarini, named for the Sun. It is a village temple of the Dravidian tradition.
sections.legends: Tradition holds that the Lord here is Ranganatha of Srirangam, who came to Thirunangur at Shiva's request, as part of the shared legend of Vishnu's eleven forms. Another telling relates to the Varaha avatara: Sridevi and Bhudevi, fearing separation, are said to have been kept company here by the Lord at rest, while his Varaha form went to vanquish Hiranyaksha. The Surya Pushkarini recalls the tale that Surya and Chandra, frightened when Shiva danced at Nangur, hid in two tanks — the Surya Pushkarini here and the Chandra Pushkarini at Thirumanikkoodam.
sections.festivals: Garuda Sevai is held the day after Thai Amavasai in the Tamil month of Thai, when the utsavars of all eleven shrines are carried on Garuda vahanams to Thirumanimadam. The Thirumangai Alvar mangalasasana utsavam is also kept in Thai. Confirm dates locally each year.
sections.experience: Among the eleven Thirunangur shrines, this is the one to visit for the sight of the reclining Lord, calm and red-eyed, with Sridevi and Bhudevi beside him. Walk to the Surya Pushkarini, and ask the priests about the title ambalam. Pilgrims familiar with Srirangam often find the sayana darshan here moving in its quiet village setting.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; the Thai Garuda Sevai is the busiest day. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Thirunangur lies about 8 km east of Sirkazhi, on the road towards Thiruvenkadu in Mayiladuthurai district. Sirkazhi has a railway station on the Chennai–Chidambaram–Mayiladuthurai line; the major airports are Tiruchirappalli and Chennai. Take a taxi or autorickshaw from Sirkazhi, since the eleven shrines lie close together.
